title: Learned about vLLM for AI Inference
description: Studied `vLLM`, an open-source library for high-throughput and memory-efficient LLM inference. Followed the tutorial from Vizuara (https://youtu.be/QyHHbeXqgrQ).

title: Revised Python Basics via NPTEL
description: Completed a revision of core Python concepts using the NPTEL tutorial (https://youtu.be/cF025BechXo). Key topics included loops, list comprehensions, and standard functions.

title: Lifecycle of a Prompt During Inference and MAX Serve Architecture
description:
Explored the end-to-end lifecycle of a prompt/request within Modular's open-source MAX Serve inference server. Key topics included:

* **Dual-process architecture**: API Server (request handling, preprocessing, tokenization) and Model Worker (GPU execution).
* **State management**: `TextContext` and `TokenBuffer` tracking.
* **Scheduling**: Prefix caching and chunked prefill.
* **GPU Pipeline**: High-throughput streaming response formatting.

Video reference: https://youtu.be/hewZwTwDBcM

title: Free Access to NVIDIA GPUs for Learning via Google Colab and Kaggle
description: Today I learned that free access to **NVIDIA GPUs** is available for learning and educational purposes through platforms such as **Google Colab** and **Kaggle**. This valuable insight was gained during a conversation with Grok.

title: Introduction to GPU Programming and LLM Attention Mechanism Optimizations
description:
This marked the first day of exploring **GPU programming**. Developed an initial understanding of the fundamental differences between the GPU execution paradigm and traditional sequential **CPU** processing. Reviewed sequential matrix multiplication and examined its critical importance in AI computations by studying the technical blog on NVIDIA's Blackwell architecture: [Matrix Multiplication on NVIDIA's Blackwell (Part 1: Introduction)](https://www.modular.com/blog/matrix-multiplication-on-nvidias-blackwell-part-1-introduction).

Additionally, viewed a YouTube video discussing the advantages of building large language models from scratch. Key technical insights included:

- In many modern LLMs, **Multi-Head Attention (MHA)** has been replaced by **Grouped Query Attention (GQA)**. This architectural change significantly reduces the size of the **KV cache**, which is particularly advantageous when handling longer context lengths.
- The combination of **Multi-Head Attention** with **sliding window attention** further contributes to substantial reductions in KV cache memory requirements.

Video reference: https://youtu.be/TXzQ7PGpO6w

title: Started Learning Language Models from Scratch with Stanford CS336
description:
Today I initiated a focused effort to understand and construct language models from the ground up to enhance my knowledge and practical skills in AI.

I began with **Stanford CS336: Language Modeling from Scratch** (Spring 2026), specifically **Lecture 1: Overview and Tokenization** presented by Percy Liang.

This course provides a comprehensive, hands-on approach to building language models, covering the complete pipeline from data preparation and tokenization through model architecture, training systems, scaling laws, inference, and post-training alignment techniques.

Key aspects of the learning plan:
- Building foundational understanding by implementing components from scratch.
- Following a structured university-level curriculum designed for end-to-end language model development.
- Progressing through lectures on tokenization, PyTorch resource accounting, Transformer architectures, systems optimizations, scaling, and alignment.

This endeavor directly supports my goal of deepening expertise in frontier AI systems through deliberate, from-scratch implementation.

title: GPU Architecture Fundamentals: Streaming Multiprocessors, Memory Hierarchy, and Thread-Block-Grid Model
description:
Today I learned core concepts of **GPU architecture** essential for high-performance computing and AI workloads.

From the educational video (https://youtu.be/HXOtJOoNF2k), I developed a clearer understanding of:

- **Streaming Multiprocessors (SMs)**: The primary processing units within NVIDIA GPUs that execute large numbers of threads concurrently.
- **Memory Hierarchy**: The layered memory system including global memory (high latency, high capacity), shared memory (low latency, block-local), registers, and constant memory, along with their impact on performance.
- **CUDA Programming Model**: The hierarchical structure of grids, blocks, and threads. A grid comprises multiple blocks, and each block contains multiple threads that execute on the same SM. Proper organization of threads and blocks is critical for achieving high occupancy and efficient memory access patterns.

These fundamentals are foundational for writing optimized parallel kernels, understanding thread scheduling, and diagnosing performance issues in GPU-accelerated applications such as deep learning and scientific computing.
